episodes.169098: An isolated thunderstorm produced localized wind damage over a portion of Hardy County.
episodes.169249: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Custer County, producing hail to golf ball size south of Fairburn.
episodes.169251: A line of thunderstorms strengthened briefly over western Mellette County, producing large hail and wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.169402: Outflow boundaries originating from distant thunderstorms converged on the valley floor during the evening hours. This combined with a pocket of upper-level divergence as analyzed by the SPC mesoanalysis resulted in the development of a strong thunderstorm over Chandler. Other weaker thunderstorms developed across the valley as well from the resulting outflow boundaries. A strong thunderstorm that developed near Morristown caused downed powerlines, resulting in the closure of US-60. No injuries were reported.
episodes.169455: A weak flow of monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over Mohave County. One storm produced severe wind.
episodes.169642: An isolated thunderstorm produced wind gusts that blew down a few trees in White Pine.
episodes.169884: Several intense clusters of storms moved through eastern Iowa into Illinois. The morning cluster produced flash flooding. In the afternoon and evening, a cluster of intense thunderstorms moved through far eastern Iowa into west central and northwest Illinois the evening of June 25th, with torrential rainfall and wind damage along it's way.
episodes.169886: Several intense clusters of storms moved through eastern Iowa into Illinois. The morning cluster produced flash flooding. In the afternoon and evening, a cluster of intense thunderstorms moved through far eastern Iowa into west central and northwest Illinois the evening of June 25th, with torrential rainfall and wind damage along it's way.
episodes.169936: Heavy rain in the Santa Fe, New Mexico area on June 25, 2022, caused minor flash flooding in the city with the arroyos filling up with water. Unfortunately, this resulted in the first arroyo flash flood fatality of the year after a man was found dead within an arroyo. However, there were other factors that contributed to his death.
episodes.170232: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening across central South Dakota, in association with an area of low pressure and cold front in a hot and muggy environment. Large hail was the main hazard, with stones ranging from quarter to tennis ball size. A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms then developed across northeastern South Dakota during the late evening, and these produced straight-line wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.170233: A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northeastern South Dakota during the late evening in association with an area of low pressure and cold front in a hot and muggy environment, and then moved east into west central Minnesota. These storms produced a measured wind gust of 67 mph seven miles southwest of Wheaton.
episodes.170239: A cold front encroaching on the Lower Ohio Valley on the warm and muggy day of June 22nd led to strong thunderstorms developing in eastern Kentucky. Storms were primarily driven by daytime heating and quickly diminished after sunset as the front pressed eastward. The strongest storms steered away from eastern Kentucky, but there were two instances of single trees down in Greenup and Lawrence Counties.
episodes.170241: Daytime heating and an abundance of moisture stirred up afternoon showers and thunderstorms across West Virginia from June 25th to the 27th. The first round of convection on the 25th resulted in several trees down around Central West Virginia while flash flooding took center stage on the 26th and 27th. The town of Flatwoods observed flooding of local businesses as a result of Granny Creek rising out of its banks from all the heavy downpours within passing thunderstorms.
episodes.170345: Mainly between 10:30 p.m. CDT on Friday the 24th and 2 a.m. CDT on Saturday the 25th, a small but potent complex of strong to severe thunderstorms tracked from southwestern into east-central portions of South Central Nebraska, prompting a few instances of marginally-severe wind gusts. The brunt of this complex affected areas between Interstate 80 and the Nebraska-Kansas state line, where numerous measured gusts of 45-55 MPH occurred. A few gusts reached or exceeded severe limits before activity abruptly weakened over northern York/southern Polk counties. The peak measured gust of 63 MPH occurred at two spots, near Holbrook in Furnas County and near Atlanta in Phelps County.||West-southwesterly flow prevailed in the upper levels, as broad high pressure was in place over southern and eastern portions of the CONUS. To the northwest, an area of low pressure was sliding east into central Canada, with a trough axis extending south into the Rockies and eventually the Plains. At the surface, the local area had east-southeasterly winds in place, with a trough axis extending through western Nebraska and Kansas between weak areas of low pressure.  With better forcing to the north and west and warm mid-level temperatures keeping things capped, the daytime and early-mid evening hours remained dry. Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours along the surface trough axis over western Nebraska, eventually pushing east into South Central Nebraska after dark. Though the better upper level lift focused well to the north, an increasing low-level jet and warm air advection aided in sustaining this slightly elevated activity as it shifted east through portions of the local area. While mesoscale analysis showed most-unstable CAPE values exceeding 3000 J/kg, deep layer shear was rather weak, around 20-30 knots.
episodes.170393: An upper level trough produced widespread showers and thunderstorms across the Midwest. Meanwhile, isolated storms developed behind the primary area of convection while instability remained high and shear was still in place to help organize storms. Most of these remained sub severe, however one storm just south of Des Moines produced up to golf ball sized hail. Later that evening a cold front swept across the area. A few non sever thunderstorms developed along the front, one of which produced a brief funnel cloud in northeast Iowa.
episodes.170595: A surface trough, draped across the western Sandhills, served as the focal point for thunderstorm development. Storms tracked east into southwestern Nebraska where they became severe. Hail up to golf ball size was reported in western Lincoln and thunderstorm wind gusts approached 70 MPH in Keith county.
episodes.170931: A deepening low pressure system over the Northern Plains moved northeast across the Northland late on the 24th. Fueled by strong southerly flow, the thunderstorm complex began to bow as the cold front advanced to the east. This line of storms produced damaging winds which lead to many trees downed and power outages across northern Minnesota.
episodes.170974: With elevated CAPE of 2500-3000 J/kg and minimal wind shear, rapidly developing updrafts resulted in periodic large hail and spotty damaging wind as storms moved along the Missouri River.
episodes.170975: An arc of thunderstorms developed along the nose of the low-level jet across northwest Iowa during the very early hours of June 25.  The thunderstorms became nearly stationary for a couple hours, and produced a very narrow band of heavy rainfall with spotty flash flooding.
episodes.171009: A few thunderstorms developed behind a cold front across portions of western Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 25th with a few reports of large hail received.
episodes.171020: In the afternoon of June 24th, a single cell thunderstorm formed in eastern Colorado, near the Colorado and Kansas border. This storm split into two with the right section heading slightly north of east into Greely County, KS while the left section moved north-northwest into Cheyenne County, CO.  The Cheyenne County storms produced hail up to nickel size. As these storms began dissipating, a line of thunderstorms formed in northeast Colorado and moved east-northeast. These storms extended from east central Colorado into west central Nebraska. Once the line of developing storms caught up to the remnants of the first storms, the line intensified. Over the next few hours in Colorado these storms produced more nickel sized hail and winds up to 61 mph.
episodes.171021: In the afternoon of June 24th, a single cell thunderstorm formed in eastern Colorado, near the Colorado and Kansas border. This storm split into two with the right section heading slightly north of east into Greely County, KS while the left section moved north-northwest into Cheyenne County, CO. The Greeley County storm produced hail up to penny size. As these storms began dissipating, a line of thunderstorms formed in northeast Colorado and moved east-northeast. These storms extended from east central Colorado into west central Nebraska. Once the line of developing storms caught up to the remnants of the first storms, the line intensified. Over the next few hours in Kansas these storms produced more penny sized hail.
episodes.171022: In the afternoon of June 24th, a single cell thunderstorm formed in eastern Colorado, near the Colorado and Kansas border. This storm split into two with the right section heading slightly north of east into Greely County, KS while the left section moved north-northwest into Cheyenne County, CO.  As these storms started dissipating, a line of thunderstorms formed in northeast Colorado and moved east-northeast. These storms extended from east central Colorado into west central Nebraska. Once the line of developing storms caught up to the remnants of the first storms, which had spread into portions of southwestern Nebraska, the line intensified. Over the next few hours in Nebraska these storms produced more nickel sized hail and severe winds. In addition, a landspout tornado occurred just north of Benkelman, NE in Dundy County.
episodes.171042: A weak upper level disturbance combined with adequate moisture, instability and wind shear to produce scattered storms in the southeast Texas Panhandle during the late afternoon into evening of the 25th. One of these storms developed into a supercell over northeastern Donley County. This storm produced a few reports of large hail and severe wind gusts.
episodes.171057: An early morning storm produced a few hail reports in Butler County.
episodes.171269: Thunderstorms formed along and near a warm front draped through central North Dakota during the afternoon and early evening hours, with many becoming severe. Early in the event, a tornado formed over south central Wells County, north of Chaseley. The tornado impacted no structures and so there was no damage to evaluate, so was rated EF Unknown by NWS policy. Heavy rains over northeast Wells County led to flash flooding, with water flowing over County Highway 5. Elsewhere, large hail was the primary threat, though there were also some occurrences of severe wind gusts. The largest hail reported was the size of a golf ball, which occurred in Stutsman County. The highest wind gust was measured at 70 mph in Kidder County.
episodes.171415: A land spout tornado was seen northeast of Prescott Valley on June 25.
episodes.171530: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were scattered reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.171580: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with a few strong thunderstorms producing wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.171655: A frontal system over Central Florida and moist, unstable air to the south across the southern Florida peninsula led to the development of scattered to numerous thunderstorms, some with torrential rainfall which led to localized flooding and frequent lightning strikes.
episodes.171741: Strong thunderstorms developed across southwest Alabama and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.171768: A plume of moisture associated with a mid-level system began to move into the region from Florida. This abundant moisture yielded fairly expansive coverage compared to previous days but with most of the moisture being in the mid levels, most storms were outflow dominant. That meant the threat for gusty winds was elevated and one storm���s outflow winds reached severe limits.
episodes.171793: Two rounds of severe thunderstorms produced large hail and gusty winds across the northern Red River Valley and into northwest Minnesota. Hail up to 2.75 inches was reported.
episodes.171794: Two rounds of severe thunderstorms produced large hail and gusty winds across the northern Red River Valley and into northwest Minnesota. Hail up to 2.75 inches was reported.
episodes.171873: Summertime convection produced scattered severe thunderstorms with reports of damaging winds and hail. In addition, pockets of heavy rainfall fell over portions of western and central Georgia, ranging from 2 to 4 inches in a short period of time. Just outside of Byron in Peach County, a single report of flash flooding was received.
